summary: Tokenizer change in canary invalidates KV-cache, triggers fallback loop and billing surge for tenant
description:
Issue summary:
During a staged canary rollout of open-llm-xlarge-v1 -> open-llm-xlarge-v1+tokenizer-fix for customer LexaHealth (dedicated pool), tenant sessions observed repeated fallback between canary and legacy variants. The canary introduces a subtle tokenizer normalization change which causes KV-cache lookups to miss; missed lookups trigger short-lived prewarm + fallback logic that resends requests to legacy variant. This creates duplicate token generation and an amplification loop that increased token consumption and caused a billing spike for the tenant.

Impact:
- Several tenants of LexaHealth saw doubled token billing for a 90-minute window.
- Intermittent mixed outputs: some requests returned responses from canary, others from legacy, causing inconsistent replies in end-user flows.
- Latency increased for affected tenant sessions (~200-400ms p95 increase).

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (redwood-dedicated-us-east-lexa-01)
- Control plane: prod-us-east
impact: Billing spike (~2x token usage) for customer LexaHealth; degraded output consistency and increased latency for affected sessions.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Have LexaHealth tenant routed to staged canary weight 10% for open-llm-xlarge-v1+tokenizer-fix.
2) Replay a set of long chat sessions that reuse KV cache (multi-turn > 6 turns) with prompt normalization that includes special punctuation sequences.
3) Observe control-plane logs: canary replies missing KV hit markers followed by fallback routing of same request to legacy variant.
4) Observe doubled token count in per-request accounting and duplicated generation calls in serving runtime logs.
logs:
Excerpt from serving-runtime (2026-03-10T14:22:17Z):
- [canary] kv_cache_lookup miss key=conv-lexa:session-9f7a turn=7 len_prefix=512
- trigger_pre_warm(canary)
- fallback_route selected -> legacy variant id=open-llm-xlarge-v1
- generation_start legacy -> token_count accounted: 264
- generation_start canary (duplicate) -> token_count accounted: 258

Edge-proxy trace (same timeline):
- client->edge request-id=abc123 forwarded to canary
- canary returned 502?cache_miss? immediate fallback to legacy per fallback-policy

Billing ledger sample: tenant-lexa token-usage 2026-03-10T14:00-15:30 increased from baseline 1.1M tokens/hr -> 2.2M tokens/hr
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: tokenizer normalization change caused cache key mismatch. Verified via diffs between tokenizer versions in PR #4492. Found that the canary strips zero-width joiners in prompts, while legacy preserves them, resulting in different serialization for KV keys.

Control plane routing: fallback logic is triggered when KV cache miss coincides with prewarm inability to satisfy latency SLO; fallback fires and replays to legacy. Because the canary and legacy have different tokenizers, the second request results in different token accounting and sometimes different completion shapes.

Observed additional amplification factor: some requests were re-enqueued by the ingress retry (edge-proxy) on a transient 504 from the canary prewarm path; that caused triple-generation in a small subset (~4% of affected requests).

Relevant links and artifacts:
- Slack: #support-lexahealth thread (message link: slack://channel/support-lexahealth/1623)
- Github PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4492
- Control-plane trace: http://grafana.internal/traces/trace-lexa-20260310-abc123
comments: Aisha Carter (Support): Initial report from LexaHealth at 2026-03-10 14:45. Customer noticed doubled bill and inconsistent chatbot replies.
Mateo Ruiz (Oncall Eng): Confirmed cache-miss pattern and fallback replays in serving logs. Flagged as P1. Created hotfix branch to make tokenizer change opt-in behind model-variant flag.
Priya Sharma (SRE): Observed edge-proxy retries correlated with increased 504s to canary prewarm endpoints; investigating connection pool exhaustion on dedicated pool.
Mateo Ruiz (Oncall Eng): Mitigation applied: reduced canary weight to 0%, disabled aggressive fallback-on-miss path for LexaHealth tenant via per-tenant policy. Notified customer.
resolution:
Mitigation steps performed 2026-03-10 -> 2026-03-11:
- Canary weight immediately rolled back to 0% for open-llm-xlarge-v1+tokenizer-fix for LexaHealth.
- Added per-tenant fallback suppression flag to prevent immediate legacy replay on KV-cache miss while we validate tokenizer behavior.
- Rolled a hotfix that makes tokenizer normalization changes gated by a model-variant flag and adds a KV-cache compatibility test in CI.
- Throttle configuration patched in edge-proxy to avoid retry storms on transient prewarm 5xxs.

Follow-ups:
- Engineering to add automated KV-cache-key equivalence checks when tokenizer binaries change (owner: Priya Sharma).
- Product to coordinate with LexaHealth on a retro and billing reconciliation (owner: CS Manager Rowan Lee).
- Billing flagged for potential credit to customer for the 90-minute amplification window (ticket created with Finance).
next_steps:
1) Deploy KV-cache compatibility unit in preflight checks (ETA 2026-03-18).
2) Engineering to add telemetry for per-request generation counts to detect amplification loops automatically (ETA 2026-03-24).
3) CS to schedule customer retro and billing reconciliation (ETA 2026-03-15).
notes: This ticket captures combined operational, billing, and model-variant interaction issues. Keeps timeline and artifacts for follow-up engineering and CS actions.
